related_questions.question: Does Medicare Part B cover vaccines?

text_blocks.snippet: Medicare Part B generally covers certain preventive vaccines like flu, pneumonia, and COVID-19 shots, as well as vaccines needed after potential exposure to a disease. It also covers the Hepatitis B vaccine for those at intermediate or high risk of contracting the virus.
snippet_highlighted_words: Medicare Part B generally covers certain preventive vaccines like flu, pneumonia, and COVID-19 shots, as well as vaccines needed after potential exposure to a disease

list.title: Preventive Vaccines:
list.snippet: Part B covers the influenza (flu) vaccine annually, the pneumococcal (pneumonia) vaccine, and the COVID-19 vaccine.

list.title: Vaccines After Exposure:
list.snippet: If you're exposed to a disease, Part B covers vaccines like tetanus (e.g., after a rusty nail injury) or rabies (e.g., after a bite).

list.title: Hepatitis B:
list.snippet: Part B covers the Hepatitis B vaccine for those at intermediate or high risk.

list.title: No Cost-Sharing:
list.snippet: For these covered vaccines, you generally don't pay anything out-of-pocket, meaning no deductibles, copayments, or coinsurance, according to Medicare resources.

list.title: Part D Coverage:
list.snippet: Other vaccines, like the shingles vaccine or the RSV vaccine for adults 60 and older, are typically covered under Medicare Part D, which is for prescription drugs.

list.title: Other Immunizations:
list.snippet: Medicare Part B may also cover other immunizations or vaccines, but these may have certain restrictions or require specific eligibility criteria.
